correctness.rationale: A bi-infinite inverse of periodic target word w corresponds to a bi-infinite path on the four de Bruijn two-bit states labeled w, hence an R_w directed cycle. A predecessor of period dividing mn exists iff R_w^m has a diagonal entry. Every four-vertex directed graph cycle has a simple cycle of length in {1,2,3,4}, hence m=12 works for all words and rules. BFS of the Boolean relation monoid generated by R_0,R_1 is exhaustive regardless of target length n; each relation is among 2^16 possible 4x4 matrices. Independently reimplemented 4-row Boolean bitmask composition, enumerated all 256 relation monoids (maximum observed size 2375), and obtained exactly {1:156,2:82,4:6,6:12}, including identical explicit rule lists. Rule 90 w=1 forces divisibility by 4; Rule 30 w=1 and w=011 force factors 3 and 2, so no global multiplier below 12. This is a complete finite state-space proof method, not extrapolation from short-ring experiments.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Prior paper bounds for bipermutive linear cases and surjective CA do not cover all 256 including nonsurjective; the earlier 16-rule and individual-rule exact theorems are strict subclasses and do not imply counts for all remaining rules.
